cur:catacombs-agape-crescentianus-sarcop.summary: Under a lid inscribed for the married couple Agape and Crescentianus, the chest is divided by twisted columns and gables into seven niches, each holding a biblical scene with Christ, the apostles or Old Testament figures. The architectural frame lends each episode the dignity of a small shrine.
facts: The lid inscription begins 'CONIVGI CARISSIMAE AGAPENI', naming Agape, who was buried by her husband Crescentianus.
Commons records the sarcophagus as coming from the Vatican necropolis.
cur:catacombs-agape-crescentianus-sarcop.notes: The individual scenes in each niche have not been verified one by one here.

wga:zearly/1/1sculptu/various/7statue3.summary: A beardless young Christ, with long curls falling to his shoulders, sits on a draped chair in tunic, pallium and sandals, holding a partly opened scroll; his right forearm, once raised in a speaking gesture, is lost. Modelled on the seated philosopher and on enthroned deities, the statuette presents Christ as the teacher of true wisdom, a type that would later grow into Christ in Majesty.
facts: Freestanding statues of Christ are extremely rare in early Christian art; this is one of the best-known.
The statuette is about 72 cm high; it was long dated c. 350–360 by comparison with the Christ of the Junius Bassus sarcophagus, while other scholars favour c. 370–380 on stylistic grounds.

wga:zearly/1/1sculptu/various/7statue3.notes: Dates in the literature range from c. 300 to the 390s; WGA's 350–75 sits within the mainstream range. Whether it is a western work or an eastern import is debated. An older catalogue reportedly described it as a seated poetess; not verified.
